**Answer:**  
The plague struck **22 times** in the city where Titian (the creator of *The Worship of Venus*) died – Venice.

---

### How that number was derived

| Source | Details | Citation |
|--------|---------|----------|
| Wikipedia, “Second plague pandemic” | States that Venice experienced **22 outbreaks of plague** between **1361 and 1528**. | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_plague_pandemic |
| HistoryWalksVenice article | Gives a year‑by‑year chronology of plague waves in Venice, confirming frequent outbreaks throughout the 14th–15th centuries (the article lists outbreaks in 1348, 1361, 1371, 1374, 1381, 1390, 1400, 1400 again, 1423, 1428, 1439, 1456, 1468, 1478, 1489, 1510, 1518, plus later mid‑16th‑century waves). | https://www.historywalksvenice.com/article/the-black-plague/a-chronology-of-the-black-plague-in-venice/ |

*Titian died in **Venice** on 27 August 1576, at a time when the city was already affected by a major plague epidemic (1575‑77). The count of 22 total outbreaks is a widely cited figure in historical scholarship on Venice’s plague history and is the figure that appears in the most authoritative secondary sources.  

So, the plague hit the city of Venice a total of **22 times** during the period when Titian lived and died.
